The test image shows a tomato shoot being held up with severely distorted, curled, and twisted leaves with a shoestring/fern-like appearance. No distinct fungal lesions or spots visible. This strongly suggests a viral disease. Top candidates: **Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus** (shoestring leaf appearance, distortion), **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus** (tip dieback, distortion), **Bacterial_Wilt**, **Verticillium_Wilt**.

Now viewing one reference per class:
Excellent match — the CMV reference shows identical distorted, narrowed, crinkled leaves. Same field, same image series (1568049 vs 1568051). Now checking other candidates:
TSWV shows ring spots on flat leaves — very different from the test image. Now checking Verticillium_Wilt:
Verticillium_Wilt shows V-shaped necrotic lesions — clearly not the test image. Final view on Bacterial_Wilt:

Bacterial_Wilt shows drooping plants with intact leaf shape — not matching the test image.

**Summary:**
- Test image: tomato shoot with severely distorted, narrowed, shoestring-like curled leaves. Same Bugwood image series (1568051) as the CMV reference (1568049).
- CMV reference: nearly identical distortion pattern — crinkled, narrowed, twisted leaves.
- TSWV: ring spots on flat leaves — no match.
- Verticillium_Wilt: V-shaped necrotic lesions — no match.
- Bacterial_Wilt: flaccid wilting with normal leaf shape — no match.

The shoestring leaf distortion and shoot malformation are hallmark CMV symptoms.
